name: 2-Wire Dimmer Switch

steps.text: At the electrical panel, turn off the circuit breakers feeding the wall box and make sure the power is off.
Remove the wall plate, unscrew the switch you are replacing and gently pull it out.
Disconnect the wires from the switch.
Making sure the wires are not touching, turn the breaker back on.
Use a voltage meter to identify the line, load and ground wires.
Turn the breaker back off.
Using the included wire nuts, connect the bare copper switch wire to ground, the red wire to the light (load) and the black wire to line.
With the LED bar on the left, gently place the switch into the wall box and screw it into place.
Turn the breaker on.
steps.expect: The light turns on and the LED shows its brightness.

steps.text: Toggle the light on and off to check that the switch works.
Reinstall the wall plate.

notes: No neutral wire is required: the switch connects to line, load and ground only.
The switch controls incandescent loads between 25W and 600W.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.

notes: As a controller: after the switch beeps, adjust the responder to the desired brightness or state and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps. The switch's LED stops blinking and it double-beeps.
As a responder: press and hold the controller button until it beeps, adjust the switch to the desired brightness (or off), then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps.
A link is one way. To keep two devices in sync (a group, such as a virtual 3-way circuit), link them in both directions.
If either LED keeps blinking, linking failed; tap that device's SET button until the LED stops blinking and try again.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, adjust it to the desired scene brightness or state, then press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps.
Tap the SET button.
steps.expect: The switch beeps and its LED stops blinking.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until the switch beeps.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
steps.expect: The switch double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

notes: To remove the switch as a responder: press and hold the controller button until it beeps, press and hold it again until it beeps, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps.

To remove several responders at once: hold the SET button until it beeps, hold it again until it beeps, then tap it (LED double-blinks red); hold each responder's SET button until it double-beeps; tap the switch's SET button to finish.

steps.text: Pull out the SET button to create an air gap, which removes power from the switch.
Press and hold in the SET button. Do not let go.
When the beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the switch double-beeps, turns on and its LED turns white.

steps.text: Remove the switch as a controller of each of its responders.
Remove the switch's responder links from all controllers.
Uninstall the switch.

notes: Otherwise controllers retry commands repeatedly, creating network delays.
In the SwitchLinc 2-Wire Dimmer Developer Notes, Set Operating Flags cmd2 0x0C to 0x0F repeat the LED on transmit and resume dim settings, and 0x10, 0x11 and 0x18 to 0x1D aren't used.

When its SET button is held, the dimmer broadcasts cmd1 0x01 with its category, subcategory and firmware in the To address; holding it again, to unlink, sends cmd1 0x02. The SwitchLinc 2-Wire Dimmer Developer Notes' example uses flags 0xCF and cmd2 0x01, the group; the Insteon Developer's Guide gives flags 0x8F and cmd2 0xFF, and makes cmd1 0x02 a controller's SET button rather than unlinking. An ID Request (cmd1 0x10) gets the same cmd1 0x01 broadcast with cmd2 0x00.

The SwitchLinc 2-Wire Dimmer Developer Notes list no operating flags readings 0x02 to 0x04, no bits 6 and 7 in the 0x00 reply, no X10 bytes in the extended Get reply, and no X10 address or retries writes, though they keep the X10 disable and enable commands and the 0x05 X10 bit.
The SwitchLinc 2-Wire Dimmer Developer Notes send D1 0x00 in the ramp rate and on-level Sets and say other values are ignored; the catalog's settings send 0x01, as for other products.
